topics.title: Money as a Medium of Exchange

concepts.learning_objective: Explain double coincidence of wants as the essential feature, and difficulty, of a barter system.
Explain how money acts as an intermediate in exchange and removes the need for double coincidence of wants.
Explain why modern currency, though of no use in itself, is accepted as a medium of exchange in India.
Explain demand deposits and how cheque payments against them settle transactions without cash.
Describe how banks use deposits to give loans and mediate between depositors and borrowers.
Explain why banks hold only a small share of deposits as cash and how they earn their main income.
Define credit and explain how it helps meet the working capital needs of production.
Analyse how risk and the absence of support in case of loss can push a borrower into a debt trap.
Define collateral and explain why lenders ask for it.
Identify the components of terms of credit and compare credit arrangements using them.
Compare the sources and terms of credit available to different people in a village.
Describe how cooperative societies raise funds and provide loans to their members.
Distinguish formal from informal sources of credit and explain the effects of high-cost informal credit.
Describe how the Reserve Bank of India supervises the functioning of formal lenders.
Analyse why richer households get a larger share of formal credit than poorer households.
Explain how Self Help Groups work and how they help the poor overcome the lack of collateral.
Describe the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh as an example of reaching the poor with credit.
